dedupe_keys.name: opus integrated assessment model for satellites and orbital debris

description: OPUS (Orbital Debris Propagators Unified with Economic Systems) is an experimental integrated assessment model that combines the astrodynamics of the orbital population with the economic behaviour of space actors, to help policymakers test proposals for managing satellite congestion and large constellations. For a set of parameters it uses an astrodynamic propagator to compute the state of objects in orbit, then applies user-defined economic and policy parameters such as launch prices and disposal regulations to model how operators respond, iterating over time; the MIT Orbital Capacity Tool (MOCAT-4S) is the main propagator, with a Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density filter shown as an alternative. It covers low Earth orbit scenarios set in CSV files, starting from historical two-line element data. It was described by Akhil Rao, Mark Moretto, Marcus Holzinger, Daniel Kaffine and Brian Weeden in arXiv 2309.10252 (September 2023), and the code is on GitHub, with the core solver in MATLAB, post-processing in R and Bash driver scripts. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article is CC-BY-SA-4.0. Caveats: the authors call it experimental, and results depend on the propagator and on assumed economic parameters. It supports optimisation and policy analysis of orbital capacity and collision cascade risk; a related record is the MIT Orbital Capacity Assessment Tool.
